findings.text: Texas does not use one statewide general-contractor licensing system. TDLR licenses specialty trades. TSBPE licenses plumbing. Many builders are regulated only locally. Do not treat this page as a count of all Texas contractors.

TDLR All Licenses on data.texas.gov (7358-krk7) has 983,494 rows. 391,308 are person trade credentials and 554,352 are other TDLR programs (cosmetology, barbering, towing, and similar). Only 37,834 Socrata rows are construction-business contractor types. That 983,494 figure is not a Texas contractor census.

Native TDLR contractor/company files acquired 38,922 business-contractor credential rows / 38,915 distinct TX-TDLR keys (A/C, electrical, sign, appliance, water well, elevator, plus mold companies). TSBPE Responsible Master Plumber adds 9,360 business-facing plumbing credentials. Person licenses are counted separately.

TDLR listing files have expiration dates, not CURRENT/REVOKED flags. Versa mold/solar/EV files and TSBPE lists publish source-native status labels. Expired is not disciplined. CURRENT_BY_EXPIRATION is not TrustHub Verified.

Comptroller active CMBL/VetHUB web_name.csv has 12,000 vendor rows. Construction-related vendors in this harvest: 3,337 (NIGP 909/910/912/913/914/968 or business category 01/02). A CMBL vendor is not a contractor license. Unmatched vendors are not unlicensed contractors.
TxDOT Project Information (drau-zphx) has 8,605 project rows. construction_manager is TxDOT staff. The file has no awarded-contractor identity field. A project is not a contractor.

TCEQ Central Registry Central Texas fragment (msah-s2rv) has 660,535 regulated-entity rows; 71,564 carry NAICS 23* in that regional file. A TCEQ customer/RE is not a contractor license. Statewide TCEQ is not acquired.

findings.text: Texas does not use one statewide general-contractor licensing system. TDLR licenses specialty trades. TSBPE licenses plumbing. Many builders are regulated only locally. Do not treat this page as a count of all Texas contractors.

TDLR All Licenses on data.texas.gov (7358-krk7) has 983,494 rows. 391,308 are person trade credentials and 554,352 are other TDLR programs (cosmetology, barbering, towing, and similar). Only 37,834 Socrata rows are construction-business contractor types. That 983,494 figure is not a Texas contractor census.

Native TDLR contractor/company files acquired 38,922 business-contractor credential rows / 38,915 distinct TX-TDLR keys (A/C, electrical, sign, appliance, water well, elevator, plus mold companies). TSBPE Responsible Master Plumber adds 9,360 business-facing plumbing credentials. Person licenses are counted separately.

TDLR listing files have expiration dates, not CURRENT/REVOKED flags. Versa mold/solar/EV files and TSBPE lists publish source-native status labels. Expired is not disciplined. CURRENT_BY_EXPIRATION is not TrustHub Verified.

Comptroller active CMBL/VetHUB web_name.csv has 12,000 vendor rows. Construction-related vendors in this harvest: 3,337 (NIGP 909/910/912/913/914/968 or business category 01/02). A CMBL vendor is not a contractor license. Unmatched vendors are not unlicensed contractors.
TxDOT Project Information (drau-zphx) has 8,605 project rows. construction_manager is TxDOT staff. The file has no awarded-contractor identity field. A project is not a contractor.

TCEQ Central Registry Central Texas fragment (msah-s2rv) has 660,535 regulated-entity rows; 71,564 carry NAICS 23* in that regional file. A TCEQ customer/RE is not a contractor license. Statewide TCEQ is not acquired.
